lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1678: the chase gets harder

Item six (a) of "fix all existing issues one through six": the flee
escalation, on the randoms only.

THE OWNER'S RULE, IN HIS WORDS
"on the randoms there should be a flee escalation. the ones that I'm purposely
throwing you head first into some big guy because you have to do that to
complete or progress a mission or a storyline — I don't think there should be
a progression on those, only on the randoms. I want the rest of the world to
be dangerous… if you step into danger level 3 you're going to see some big bad
guys and there is a chance you're going to get stuck having that fight that
might end the game for you."

His own log is the measurement behind it: he flees everything at ~100 HP or
more on random ground and wins the escape roll nearly every time. OTA-1009
made the flee contested (fastest pursuer's d20 + speed) and OTA-1459 made it
cost stamina, and neither moved the outcome — the bar was the same on the
first break as on the fourth, on a danger-1 verge as in a danger-5 pit, for a
rat as for a Legendary.

ON RANDOM GROUND THE PURSUER'S BAR NOW MOVES
  +1 per danger level above 1 (danger 3 → +2, danger 5 → +4)
  +0 / +1 / +2 / +3 by the pursuer's rarity
  +2 per failed break THIS encounter (2nd try +2, 3rd try +4 …)
  −2 when the pursuer is at or under half HP, −4 at or under a quarter
The one who can catch you is chosen AFTER escalation, so a bleeding sprinter
loses the chase to a fresh brute. The roll card prints the breakdown ("Pursuit
25 — Mud Wasp (d20 14 + 11: SPD 5, danger +2, Rare +2, 2nd try +2)"), a failed
break says "They have your measure now. The next break will be harder." before
the volley lands, and the FLEE chip carries the exact odds ("flee 48%"),
counted over all 400 d20 pairs — from the SAME reader the roll is built from
(state/fleeOdds), so the chip cannot promise a different chase than the tap
produces. His picture at DEX 11 (+1 Reclaimer): danger 3 vs a Rare, 66% → 57%
→ 48% over three tries; danger 5 vs a Legendary on the third try, 30%.

RANDOM IS DECLARED BY THE PRODUCER, NEVER INFERRED
There is no field on an Enemy or a scene that says "this fight is a
mission's", and there are dozens of scripted spawn sites against four world
rolls. So the four rolls stamp `Enemy.unscripted` — beginScene's encounter,
the climb encounter, the rest ambush, the patrol crossing — and every scripted
spawn (hunt stages, core guardians, chain marks, captors, summit bosses,
hostile traders, raids, hostile-ground patrols, and every body from a save
before this OTA) resolves to exactly OTA-1009's escapePursuit, asserted equal.
A lineup escalates only when EVERY live body carries the mark: a mission mark
that joins a roaming pack turns the scene scripted, which is the direction the
rule leans. The mark rides on the enemy like `pos` and `coating`, so splices,
saves and loads carry it with no bookkeeping. The failed-break count lives on
the scene (`fleeAttempts`), reset by FRESH_ENEMY_ARRAYS and by every lineup
producer, so it cannot outlive the bodies it was earned against.

Under the OTA-1400 line ratchet, `injectFactionParty` moved verbatim to
app/state/factionParty.ts (its three callers pass `scalePowerOf` in);
gameStore is at 36,914 lines.

- app/engine/fleeEscalation.ts (NEW) — the mark, the four terms, the escalated
  pursuit, the exact odds.
- app/state/fleeOdds.ts (NEW) — the one reader for the bar: the dispatch and
  the FLEE chip both go through it.
- app/state/factionParty.ts (NEW) — injectFactionParty, moved.
- app/engine/types.ts — Enemy.unscripted. app/engine/combatRules.ts —
  EscapePursuit.note, printed on the card.
- app/state/gameStore.ts — four producers stamp; the dispatch reads
  fleePursuitFor; the failed-escape arm counts and speaks; CurrentScene
  .fleeAttempts; FRESH_ENEMY_ARRAYS resets it.
- app/components/InputBox.tsx — "flee 48%".
- __tests__/ota1678TheChaseGetsHarder.test.ts — 25 tests, including the
  scripted-lineup identity with escapePursuit, the bestiary-wide worst case,
  and the producer census (exactly four stamps, no scripted site touches it).
- __tests__/ota1009, ota1116, ota1015, ota1035, ota1159, ota1321, ota1476,
  ota1506 — pins repointed to the shared reader, the moved spawner, and the
  odds-bearing FLEE label; their claims are unchanged.
